reports.title: KERMT v2 and GROVER, fine-tuned on the same folds
reports.eyebrow: Graph-transformer pre-training, with an exposure control
reports.question: Does NVIDIA's re-pretrained GROVER encoder, fine-tuned by its own code, hold up against the ADMET field — and how much of any gain survives the fact that it was pre-trained on these molecules?
reports.takeaway: The contrastive re-pretraining beats both original GROVER checkpoints, and scaling GROVER does not help at all, but none of the three reaches fine-tuned Atom-JEPA or Monroe + TabPFN 3 on Biogen. Frozen, KERMT's latent is far behind Monroe's.
reports.summary: KERMT is NVIDIA's GPU-optimised reimplementation of GROVER, a dual-view graph transformer; its released checkpoint, NV-KERMT-70M-v2, re-pretrains that encoder with a contrastive objective. All three checkpoints — v2, GROVER base and GROVER large — are fine-tuned here by KERMT's own main.py finetune, 25 fold models each, and v2's frozen 512-d latent is also read by TabPFN 3 with Monroe's call, against LightGBM, fine-tuned CheMeleon, Monroe + TabPFN 3 and fine-tuned Atom-JEPA.
reports.finding: Fine-tuned v2 beats fine-tuned GROVER base 30–13–2 over 45 endpoint x metric calls and GROVER large 33–12–0, while GROVER large against base is 3–26–16, so the larger original checkpoint is if anything the weaker one. All three beat LightGBM and fine-tuned CheMeleon, but v2 trails fine-tuned Atom-JEPA 7–11–27 and wins no Biogen call against Monroe + TabPFN 3 (0–2–16), though it is ahead of Monroe on ExpansionRx (15–1–11). No arm fitted here is ever best alone in a Tukey tier. Frozen under TabPFN 3, v2's latent is behind Monroe's on 13 of 15 endpoints and wins 3 of 45 calls; fine-tuning beats it 41–4–0.
reports.caveat: The released v2 checkpoint was pre-trained on a corpus containing every ExpansionRx and Biogen molecule, test rows included (structures, no labels), so the v2-vs-GROVER gap mixes better pre-training with structural exposure and this design cannot separate them; the two GROVER checkpoints pre-date these data sets and are the unexposed control. KERMT's load_checkpoint also copies the pre-trained checkpoint's saved args over the command line, so v2 trains with dropout 0.1 and selects on validation MAE while both GROVER arms train with no dropout and select on validation loss; the code was run as released and every fold records what it used.
